summary:
India's statistics ministry has proposed revisions to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) so that it captures digital platform gig work and unpaid work. The proposal responds to an ongoing debate about whether official jobs data adequately reflects underemployment and job quality in India, where headline unemployment is reported at 5%.

Key changes: a separate survey category for digital platform workers, since the existing method did not capture enough of them, and a wider set of rural and urban household respondents asked whether members do platform work. The survey will also begin measuring activities that are typically unpaid, including production of goods for own use, household and caregiving activities, volunteer work and unpaid trainee work.

Context cited: the government's economic survey in January estimated a 55% increase in gig workers in the five years to 2025-26, with such workers possibly comprising 2% of the total workforce.

Labour economist K.R. Shyam Sundar, formerly of XLRI Jamshedpur, called the platform gig worker estimation effort "a half-step" because many informal gig workers are not on any platform, but said capturing unpaid work in the PLFS is an important step that could eventually change the methodology used to calculate national income.

Timeline: the changes take effect from January 2027, with fresh samples for 2027-28. The government invited public and expert feedback within 15 days. The article notes the revisions will affect comparability with past data. Reported by Shubham Batra in New Delhi, edited by Mrigank Dhaniwala and Harikrishnan Nair, republished by Allwork.Space.

The item is macro labour-statistics news rather than workplace operations content, with no coverage of visitor management, desk or room booking, RTO policy, workplace analytics or facilities topics.
